title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
claim: A tree search over denoising steps, extended with proposal reweighting and preference-conditioned passes, steers a generative model toward single- or multi-objective targets.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; tree, proposal, 2-D objective space, 3-D tree
description: A 2x2 grid of panels labeled (a) to (d), drawn in a purple-to-teal-to-green palette. Panel (a) shows a search tree running top to bottom along a diffusion-step axis from T to 0. Node size marks expected reward, and a base density in gray sits under a reward-tilted density in green. Panel (b) shows a state x_t branching to two child samples. Beneath them are a gray base density p_θ and a green proposal density q_c, with arrows marking the reweighting and large and small dots for the resulting weights. Panel (c) is a 2-D objective space with gray base contours, purple single-preference tilted blobs, and a green curved Pareto-tilted band, with a legend. Panel (d) is a 3-D tree whose branches end at orange circled points along a dashed Pareto front. The eye goes first to the colorful tree in (a).
caption: Overview of the method. (a): DTS treats intermediate states of denoising diffusion as nodes in a tree, and steers sampling towards a reward-tilted distribution. Each node is attached to an estimate of expected reward (denoted here by node size). (b): We may use a different model $q_c$ that gives better denoising proposals, but we need to correct its influence by reweighting nodes by the proposal's ratio with the base model. (c): In the multi-objective setting, we wish to sample from a distribution obtained by integrating reward-tilted distributions over different preferences between objectives. (d): We use a single DTS tree to sample from this multi-objective target, conditioning each pass through the tree on a different preference.
abstract: Diffusion-based generative models have become strong priors over plausible crystal structures, but turning that prior into promising candidates requires steering toward several conflicting properties at once. Fine-tuning is expensive and produces a new model for every new objective, while differentiable guidance is not applicable to many real-world tasks. We instead adapt these generative models at inference time using Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure over the denoising trajectory. We make two technical contributions on top of DTS that are particularly relevant for AI-for-science applications. First, we show how to use existing property-conditional generative models (e.g., models fine-tuned for classifier-free guidance) as guided proposals inside DTS, without distorting the target distribution. Second, we extend DTS to multi-objective sampling, so that a single search produces samples spanning an entire Pareto front. We instantiate both adaptations on de novo crystal generation: improving the stability of crystals generated by different models, using pretrained conditional models to generate crystals belonging to rare space groups or with high bulk modulus, and generating crystals along a Pareto front of high dielectric constant and high bandgap materials. Across these tasks, DTS-based inference-time adaptation successfully improves model outputs without modifying the models themselves.
